title: Appliance Repair Software: Dispatch, Booking and Invoicing Tools
html:
Appliance repair software starts with booking and dispatch, because every missed call is a lost service visit. Pick a field service app such as Housecall Pro, Workiz or ServiceM8, add accounting, and build a website that wins repair searches. Published prices in this guide run from $0 to $627 a month, and Workiz does not publish a price.

Appliance repair software has to keep a van full without double booking it. A tech may run six calls in a day, each with a different brand, model and part. The tool that wins is the one that books fast, dispatches cleanly and invoices on the spot.

This guide sorts tools by the job each one does: dispatch, small-shop scheduling, invoicing, photos and books. Each tool shows the price its own vendor lists and one real limit.

Which appliance repair software dispatches techs best?

Housecall Pro, Workiz and Service Fusion all dispatch technicians and send invoices. They differ most in how they price teams and what they leave out of the listed price.

  • Housecall Pro: Basic is $59 a month billed annually or $79 monthly for one user. Essentials is $149 or $189 for five users. Max is $299 or $329 for eight users. Limit: add-ons such as campaigns and voice show no price on the page, and Max charges $35 a month for each user past eight.
  • Workiz: lists Standard, Pro and Ultimate plans with unlimited jobs, estimates and invoices on all three. Pro adds Genius Scheduling and roles and permissions, and Ultimate adds inventory, equipment tracking and service plans. Limit: no price is shown, since each plan says request pricing.
  • Service Fusion: lists Starter, Plus and Pro with unlimited users. One set of prices is $208, $325 and $533 a month billed annually, and a second set is $245, $382 and $627. Limit: add-on prices are not shown, and the page does not label the second set as monthly.

Inventory is the feature that separates these for repair work. Ultimate on Workiz lists inventory and equipment tracking, and Service Fusion lists inventory management as an add-on on Starter and included on Plus. A shop that stocks common parts such as igniters, door seals and pumps should ask each vendor how a van stock count works.

Do not buy on the headline plan alone. Ask for a quote with your real tech count, the add-ons you need and the card rate. Housecall Pro lists card processing as low as 2.59%, so the final rate depends on your account.

Which scheduling app suits a small appliance repair shop?

A one or two tech shop rarely needs a full dispatch board. ServiceM8 and Jobber give small teams scheduling, quotes and invoices at lower monthly prices.

  • ServiceM8: Free is $0 for 1 user and 30 jobs a month. Starter is $29 for 50 jobs, Growing is $79 for 150 jobs and Premium is $149 for 500 jobs, with unlimited users on paid plans. Limit: every plan caps jobs per month, and a repair visit and a return visit each count.
  • Jobber: Core is $49 a month with no commitment or $29 a month billed annually, for one user. Extra users cost $29 a month each. Limit: card payments cost 2.9% plus 30 cents, and add-ons such as Marketing Suite at $99 a month are extra.

Count visits, not customers. A washer repair that needs a part ordered is two visits, and a callback is a third. A shop with two techs doing five calls each a day books about 200 visits a month, which is beyond the ServiceM8 Growing cap.

What do repair techs use for estimates and invoices on site?

A solo tech who prices by flat rate may only need invoicing. Joist sends estimates and invoices and takes online payments from a phone.

  • Joist: Basics is $10 a month and Pro is $17 a month on monthly billing. Elite is $32 and Run is $100. Limit: Basics allows 5 documents a month, so a tech doing five calls a day passes it in a day.

Flat rate price books speed up repair quotes. Write a diagnostic fee, a labor tier and a common-part list. Show the homeowner the total before you start work, and collect payment before you leave the driveway.

Joist does not dispatch or track parts. It fits a solo operator who books by phone, and it pairs well with a free scheduling plan until volume grows.

How should an appliance repair company handle parts, warranty and callbacks?

Repair work has three loops that general scheduling tools often handle poorly: parts orders, warranty claims and callbacks. Decide how you will track each before you choose software.

  • Parts: record the part number and order date on the job, and set a follow-up for the return visit.
  • Warranty: store the model and serial number, the manufacturer claim number and the approval date in job notes or custom fields.
  • Callbacks: tag any return visit within your warranty window so you can see which techs and parts cause repeats.
  • Contracts: track service plans separately from one-time repairs, since renewals need reminders.

Ask each vendor for a demo that shows a parts order, a return visit and a warranty note on one job. If the tool needs a workaround for any of them, add the cost of that workaround to the price.

Fire protection and window cleaning shops track recurring service the same way.

Which tools keep photos and the books in order?

Two small tools close the loop: a photo app for model plates and part condition, and an accounting package for the books.

  • CompanyCam: stores timestamped photos by project. Core is $63 a month billed annually, Crew is $129 and Scale is $199, with extra users at $29. Limit: Core includes one user and caps at two.
  • QuickBooks Online: Simple Start is $19 a month for the first three months, then $38. Essentials is $42.50, then $85, and Plus is $70, then $140. Limit: users are capped at one, three and five by plan.

Photograph the model and serial plate and the failed part on every call. Store the photos on the job, not in a phone gallery, so the office can find them later. That protects you in a warranty dispute and helps the next tech who opens the job.

Which tools bring in appliance repair calls?

Software runs the visit, but calls come from search, maps and ads. Google states that creating a Business Profile is free, so a complete profile is the cheapest lead tool a repair shop can own.

Limit: a profile needs photos, accurate service areas and replies to every review.

Repair searches are urgent, so ads fill a schedule quickly. See the pricing page .

How do you choose appliance repair software for your company?

Choose appliance repair software with a three-check filter: fit, cost and setup effort. Run every tool through all three before you pay.

Fit: does it book by time window, dispatch by tech, store model and serial numbers and send an invoice from the phone?

Cost: add the plan, per-user fees, job caps and card fees, then compare the total with the revenue of one average repair visit.

Setup effort: can the owner load a price book, customers and three techs in one weekend?

Company typeStarting stackAdd next
Solo techJoist Basics or ServiceM8 Free, QuickBooks Simple Start, free Business ProfileServiceM8 Starter
Two to five techsServiceM8 Growing, Jobber Connect or Housecall Pro Essentials, QuickBooks EssentialsCompanyCam
Six or more techs, parts stockWorkiz Pro or Ultimate, Service Fusion Plus, Housecall Pro MaxMarketing support for lead flow

A solo tech should keep the stack small and learn it well. A multi-van company should run a one-week trial with every tech, because the field app decides whether the system gets used.

Software does not create demand, and a full van still needs a steady stream of calls. A website with a booking form on every page turns those visits into calls.

What do appliance repair owners get wrong when they buy software?

The first error is buying for a bigger shop. A two tech shop that signs for an eight user plan pays for seats nobody uses. Buy for the next six months, and upgrade when a real limit blocks you.

The second error is ignoring caps. A ServiceM8 plan limits jobs a month, and Housecall Pro limits users by plan. Count your real monthly visits before you pick.

The third error is forgetting the call itself. The best dispatch board does nothing if the phone goes to voicemail. Decide who answers, and how after-hours calls get a text back.

How should an appliance repair shop set up booking windows?

Booking windows decide how many calls a tech can run in a day. Set them once in the scheduling tool, and the tool protects the van from double booking.

  • Diagnostic slots: shorter windows for diagnosis, with a buffer for travel between calls.
  • Repair slots: longer windows for jobs where the part is already on the van.
  • Return visits: a separate slot type for part installs, so they are not squeezed into diagnosis time.
  • Same-day holds: a few open slots each day for urgent calls such as a dead refrigerator.

Ask each vendor whether customers can book online into those windows and whether the tech gets a text with the model and symptom. A booking form that collects brand, model and symptom saves a phone call and helps the tech bring the right part.

Review the window lengths after a month. If techs run late every day, the windows are too short. If vans sit idle, they are too long. Adjust, then check again, since the data in your own tool is a better guide than any template.

What software does an appliance repair business need?

An appliance repair business needs booking, dispatch, invoicing and payment tools. Start with a scheduling app and a free Google Business Profile. Add inventory and warranty tracking when you stock parts and handle manufacturer claims, and add photo and accounting tools as the team grows.

How much does appliance repair software cost?

Published prices in this guide start at $0 for ServiceM8 Free and $10 a month for Joist Basics. Jobber Core is $29 to $49 a month, Housecall Pro starts at $59 billed annually, and Service Fusion lists $208 to $627. Workiz does not publish a price.

Is Workiz or Housecall Pro better for appliance repair?

Both dispatch techs and send invoices. Housecall Pro publishes prices from $59 a month billed annually for one user. Workiz asks you to request pricing and lists inventory and equipment tracking on Ultimate. Compare them using your tech count and a parts workflow demo.

Is there free appliance repair software?

ServiceM8 lists a Free plan at $0 for 1 user and 30 jobs a month, with text messages at 10 cents each. That suits a solo tech starting out. A shop doing more than 30 visits a month will need a paid plan, starting at $29.

Can Jobber handle parts and warranty tracking for appliance repair?

Jobber covers scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments. It does not list parts inventory or warranty claim tracking, so use job notes or confirm the features with the vendor. Core is $49 a month with no commitment or $29 billed annually.

Do appliance repair companies need a website if they use booking software?

Yes. Booking software runs the visit after the call, but it does not bring calls in. A website with pages for each appliance type and brand, a booking form and a Google Business Profile gives homeowners a reason to choose you.

What should a new appliance repair company buy first?

Set up a free Google Business Profile and a scheduling app first. ServiceM8 Free or Joist Basics at $10 a month are cheap starts. Add dispatch, inventory and photo tools only when missed bookings or parts mix-ups start costing you visits.

Ask each vendor whether customers can book online into those windows and whether the tech gets a text with the model and symptom. A booking form that collects brand, model and symptom saves a phone call and helps the tech bring the right part.
Review the window lengths after a month. If techs run late every day, the windows are too short. If vans sit idle, they are too long. Adjust, then check again, since the data in your own tool is a better guide than any template.
###
What software does an appliance repair business need?
An appliance repair business needs booking, dispatch, invoicing and payment tools. Start with a scheduling app and a free Google Business Profile. Add inventory and warranty tracking when you stock parts and handle manufacturer claims, and add photo and accounting tools as the team grows.
###
How much does appliance repair software cost?
Published prices in this guide start at $0 for ServiceM8 Free and $10 a month for Joist Basics. Jobber Core is $29 to $49 a month, Housecall Pro starts at $59 billed annually, and Service Fusion lists $208 to $627. Workiz does not publish a price.
###
Is Workiz or Housecall Pro better for appliance repair?
Both dispatch techs and send invoices. Housecall Pro publishes prices from $59 a month billed annually for one user. Workiz asks you to request pricing and lists inventory and equipment tracking on Ultimate. Compare them using your tech count and a parts workflow demo.
###
Is there free appliance repair software?
ServiceM8 lists a Free plan at $0 for 1 user and 30 jobs a month, with text messages at 10 cents each. That suits a solo tech starting out. A shop doing more than 30 visits a month will need a paid plan, starting at $29.
###
Can Jobber handle parts and warranty tracking for appliance repair?
Jobber covers scheduling, quotes, invoices and payments. It does not list parts inventory or warranty claim tracking, so use job notes or confirm the features with the vendor. Core is $49 a month with no commitment or $29 billed annually.
###
Do appliance repair companies need a website if they use booking software?
Yes. Booking software runs the visit after the call, but it does not bring calls in. A website with pages for each appliance type and brand, a booking form and a Google Business Profile gives homeowners a reason to choose you.
###
What should a new appliance repair company buy first?
Set up a free Google Business Profile and a scheduling app first. ServiceM8 Free or Joist Basics at $10 a month are cheap starts. Add dispatch, inventory and photo tools only when missed bookings or parts mix-ups start costing you visits.
